title: Rochdale Armed Forces and Veterans Breakfast Club receives £500 from housebuilders
excerpt: Barratt and David Wilson Homes have given £500 towards the club's running costs ahead of Remembrance Day.
body:
The Rochdale Armed Forces and Veterans Breakfast Club has received a £500 donation from Barratt and David Wilson Homes towards its running costs.

The money will go towards food for members. The club is part of Armed Forces and Veterans Breakfast Clubs, a network of breakfast clubs where veterans and serving personnel meet regularly.

Dave Williamson, a director at Armed Forces and Veterans Breakfast Clubs, thanked the company for its support. He said contributions like this help keep the clubs running.

Claire Jarvis, managing director at David Wilson Homes North West, said the donation was part of the company's wider support for veterans across the region.

The club is separate from the Rochdale Veterans Breakfast Club, which meets on Thursday mornings at the Flying Horse Hotel on Packer Street, according to Rochdale Borough Council's events listing. That club was not involved in this donation.

The donation was announced shortly before Remembrance Sunday, when services were held across the borough.

corrections.note: This article originally described the recipient as the Rochdale veterans breakfast club and carried a file photograph of a different group. The donation went to the Rochdale Armed Forces and Veterans Breakfast Club, which is separate from the Rochdale Veterans Breakfast Club. The headline, text and image have been corrected, and the meeting place given in the original report has been removed.
